title: Training Notes: Courtesy Refunds of Cancellation and No-Show Fees on Wayfare Rides
content:
**The rule.** On **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)** a courtesy refund returns an on-demand cancellation fee or on-demand no-show fee that was charged correctly under the rules. Reserved late cancellation fees and reserved no-show fees, fares and all other charges are never refunded as a courtesy. A rider may receive a courtesy refund only while fewer courtesy refunds than the ride option's courtesy allowance have been booked on any of the rider's trips in the courtesy window, counted across all of the rider's trips rather than the trip in question. A fee that the rules show was charged in error is refunded under its own reason code and never counts as a courtesy refund. The driver keeps the share of a fee refunded as a courtesy; Wayfare absorbs it.

## The courtesy window

The courtesy window is a rolling window of the ride option's courtesy window length in calendar days, ending on the current day, both ends included. The count is the refunds booked with the reason *courtesy cancellation refund* on any trip of the same rider whose date falls in that window, read from the system's charge records.

## Questions the rule answers

**Which fees can a courtesy refund return?** Only an on-demand cancellation fee or an on-demand no-show fee that was charged correctly.

**Can a reserved late cancellation fee be refunded as a courtesy?** No. Neither can a reserved no-show fee, a fare, or any other charge.

**Does a courtesy refund booked on a different trip count?** Yes. The count runs across all of the rider's trips in the window, not only the trip in question.

**A no-show fee was marked before the required wait had passed. Is its refund a courtesy refund?** No. A fee the rules show was charged in error is refunded under its own reason code, and that refund does not count toward the courtesy allowance.

**Who bears a courtesy refund?** Wayfare absorbs it; the driver keeps the share of the fee.

## Worked case (hypothetical allowance of 1 in a 90-day window)

A rider's records show one courtesy cancellation refund booked 40 days ago on another trip. One is not fewer than 1, so no courtesy refund is available today. Had that refund been booked 95 days ago, it would fall outside the window, the count would be zero, and a correctly charged on-demand cancellation fee could be refunded as a courtesy.
